overview: A single State Department letter dated May 2, 1947, responding to T. J. Draper’s April 17 proposal to reestablish Standard-Vacuum Oil Company’s bunkering service in occupied Japan. Edwin M. Martin explains that the plan requires final approval from the Army-Navy Petroleum Board, after which the company’s representative in Japan may investigate the condition of its Tsurumi facilities with the knowledge and acquiescence of the Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers.

subfiles.title: Letter from Edwin M. Martin to T. J. Draper on restoring bunkering service in Japan
subfiles.from: Edwin M. Martin, Chief, Division of Japanese and Korean Economic Affairs
subfiles.to: T. J. Draper, Standard-Vacuum Oil Company
subfiles.about: Martin advises Draper of the approvals and occupation-authority acquiescence required before Standard-Vacuum can investigate and restore its bunkering facilities at Tsurumi.
subfiles.summary: Martin acknowledges Draper’s letter of April 17, 1947, describing plans to reestablish bunkering service in Japan. He states that final formal approval by the Army-Navy Petroleum Board is required before the plan can operate. Once approval is granted, Draper may direct the company’s employee in Japan to investigate the status of the Tsurumi bunkering facilities with the knowledge and acquiescence of the Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers.
keywords: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers

interest: The letter offers a compact illustration of how private American petroleum interests sought to resume operations in Japan under the Allied occupation. It is especially useful for showing the layered approval process: commercial investigation and reconstruction depended both on the Army-Navy Petroleum Board and on SCAP’s acquiescence. The reference to the preexisting Tsurumi bunkering service may help historians trace the restoration of port infrastructure, marine fuel supply, and foreign corporate activity in postwar Japan.
